berlin.name: Checkpoint Charlie
berlin.summary: The best-known Cold War crossing between East and West Berlin, now a replica guard hut and an open-air history gallery.
berlin.expect: The hut itself is a photo stop on a busy junction; the free outdoor panels along Friedrichstraße tell the story better than the paid museum.
berlin.tip: Pair it with the Topography of Terror, a seven-minute walk west along the surviving stretch of Wall.
berlin.why: Soviet and American tanks faced each other here in October 1961, one of the tensest moments of the Cold War.
flow: Read the outdoor Cold War gallery panels on the corner.
See the replica hut and the soldier portraits.
Walk west along Zimmerstraße to the Wall remnant and Topography of Terror.
berlin.best: Early morning before the tour groups
berlin.bestFor: Cold War history on a walk between Mitte and Kreuzberg

berlin.name: Berlin TV Tower
berlin.summary: East Germany's 368 m TV tower, still the tallest structure in Germany, with a viewing deck and revolving restaurant at 203 m.
berlin.expect: Timed tickets and a security check; the deck gives a full 360° view across both halves of the city.
berlin.tip: Book a timed slot online for sunset; walk-up queues can run over an hour at weekends.
berlin.why: Built in 1969 as a symbol of the GDR, it is now the clearest landmark on the Berlin skyline.
flow: Collect tickets at the base on Alexanderplatz.
Ride the lift to the 203 m viewing deck.
Walk down to Museum Island across the Spree afterwards.
berlin.bestFor: A full view of the city in one stop

berlin.name: Charlottenburg Palace
berlin.summary: Berlin's largest Prussian royal palace, with baroque state rooms, the New Wing and formal gardens along the Spree.
berlin.expect: Calmer than central sights; the gardens are free and the palace rooms are seen with an audio guide.
berlin.tip: Closed on Mondays. The gardens and Belvedere tea house are worth an extra hour on a sunny day.
berlin.why: Built for Queen Sophie Charlotte around 1700, it is the best surviving picture of Hohenzollern court life in Berlin.
flow: Start in the Old Palace state rooms.
Walk the baroque garden out to the Belvedere and mausoleum.
berlin.best: Weekday mornings, spring to autumn for the gardens
berlin.bestFor: Palace interiors and gardens away from the centre

lisbon.name: Tram 28
lisbon.summary: The old yellow Remodelado trams that rattle up Lisbon's steepest streets from Graça through Alfama and Baixa to Estrela.
lisbon.expect: Very crowded at the Martim Moniz end from mid-morning; pickpockets work the packed cars.
lisbon.tip: Board early (before 9am) at Martim Moniz, or ride the quieter Tram 12 loop for the same Alfama streets.
lisbon.why: Lisbon's hills made the narrow-gauge trams survive here when most European cities scrapped theirs.
flow: Ride up through Graça and past Miradouro de Santa Luzia.
Hop off in Chiado or ride on to Estrela Basilica.
lisbon.bestFor: Seeing the old hill neighbourhoods without climbing them

lisbon.name: Praça do Comércio
lisbon.summary: The grand riverside square rebuilt after the 1755 earthquake, framed by yellow arcades and the Rua Augusta triumphal arch.
lisbon.expect: Open and sunny with cafés under the arcades; the arch has a small paid viewing terrace.
lisbon.tip: Climb the Rua Augusta Arch for a view down the Baixa grid, then walk the riverfront to Cais do Sodré.
lisbon.why: It was the site of the royal palace destroyed in 1755 and became the showpiece of Pombal's rebuilt Lisbon.
flow: Walk down Rua Augusta through the arch.
Cross the square to the Cais das Colunas steps on the river.
Follow the waterfront west to Cais do Sodré.

lisbon.name: Lisbon Oceanarium
lisbon.summary: One of Europe's largest aquariums, built for Expo 98 around a single huge central ocean tank.
lisbon.expect: Indoor and family-friendly; weekends and rainy days are busy.
lisbon.tip: Ride the cable car along the river at Parque das Nações after your visit.
lisbon.why: Its central tank lets you see four ocean habitats from one walkway, with sunfish, rays and sharks together.
flow: Start at the upper level around the central tank.
Walk through the four ocean habitats.
Finish at the lower level windows into the main tank.
